SQL-память агента: результаты эксперимента

8 ноября 2026. Поиск отдельных механизмов, не leaderboard и не статистический accuracy benchmark.

Краткий результат

  • Найден воспроизводимый отдельный случай вреда ICL: GLM переносит ошибочный SQL-grain из раннего задания в новые. В выбранном инциденте исходный запуск и два replay с прежней историей дают неверные знаменатели; исходный fresh и два fresh-повтора дают правильные знаменатели. Рост отказов занижается с 15 до 9,12 п.п., а повторные попытки превращаются в вымышленный рост трафика.
  • Так же убедительной причинной демонстрации «память помогла дать верный ответ» не получили. Есть правильные ICL против ошибочных fresh, но это ещё не доказывает роль истории.
  • Файловая память сама по себе почти не используется. Luna/Haiku с исходной разрешающей инструкцией ничего не записывают; GLM сохраняет ответ и читает его лишь на T3. Более директивная, но общая инструкция вести заметки вызывает реальное чтение/перезапись у Luna — без гарантии правильности всех ответов.
  • Миграция не сломала основные ICL-ветки. Агенты обнаруживают новый источник. Старый запрос Haiku сначала даёт пустой результат, затем исправляется.
  • Число действий и цена расходятся. GLM ICL делает меньше действий, но стоит дороже fresh из-за контекста; у Haiku на той же задаче ICL, наоборот, дешевле.

Важное ограничение архива

После окончания всех прогонов при подготовке HTML/финальной публикации контейнер был уничтожен инструментом. Не всё удалось сохранить. Из GitHub восстановлены полные оригинальные траектории 43/45 основных попыток + 2 диагностик. Все 45 совпадают по SHA-256 с аудитом, выгруженным до сбоя. Сохранены также полный агрегированный аудит денег/токенов и все 448 shell-команд 60 валидных попыток. Полные логи остальных 15 попыток и приватные native checkpoints утрачены.

Для пяти утраченных GLM-траекторий повторно исполнены только инструменты, без модельных API: 50 сохранённых команд на БД с исходными хешами; все exit codes совпали, механизм ошибочного denominator воспроизведён. Это не восстановленные модельные диалоги. Исходные финальные числа этих попыток в тексте опираются на анализ, сделанный до сбоя; оригинальный final response доступен не везде. Подробный перечень: RECOVERY.md, recovery_inventory.json.

1. Устройство эксперимента

Использован новый синтетический стенд вместо публичных заданий CL-Bench. Генератор, seed и reference calculations заморожены до evaluation. Это снижает вероятность запоминания конкретных ответов, но не исключает знакомство с аналитическими шаблонами.

Модели: gpt-6-luna через ChatGPT/Codex Responses Lite; claude-haiku-5-5 напрямую Anthropic; z-ai/glm-5.3-flash через OpenRouter. Доступы и GitHub write проверены реальными действиями до запуска.

Режим Между заданиями
Fresh / stateless Новая сессия, никаких файлов/истории
ICL Полная native история: вопросы, tool calls/results, ответы, возвращённое reasoning-состояние
Managed / optional Новая сессия; только самостоятельно сохранённые файлы ../memory, без auto-injection

Единый инструмент — bash, обычные sqlite3/Python/cat/grep/sed; никаких bespoke memory/retrieval tools. Gold/оценки не возвращаются агентам. Все необходимые определения и факты восстановимы из текущей БД + README. Это тест памяти-кеша, не сохранения невосстановимых наблюдений.

Нет query-count reward, лимита 15 запросов или 50 строк. Tool output до 60 000 символов, с явным truncation. Guards: 80 ходов / 15 минут на задачу, 60 s shell, 45 s CPU на процесс, 600 MiB адресного пространства. Задачи и DB hashes одинаковы во всех режимах, включая fresh после миграции.

Пять заданий

ID Что проверяет
W1 Операции против попыток, retries и terminal failures; temporal joins и routing aliases
W2 Первый инцидент: уменьшенный deadline при стабильном upstream
T1 Тренд/конфаундинг: pooled improvement, но кандидат хуже во всех 8 matched strata
T2 Похожий симптом, другая причина: workers 16→4, queue 4→180, deadline неизменен
T3 Необъявленная миграция attempt→operation grain и routing intent→actual execution cell

До миграции: 20 таблиц, 32 500 операций, 40 480 попыток. После: 22 таблицы, добавлены 4 000 новых операций/outcomes. Чистые синтетические данные, маленький warehouse, явный бизнес-контракт. T1 задаёт требуемую стратификацию; это не тест самостоятельного открытия всех конфаундеров.

45 основных попыток, одна из них censored output. Ещё 15 диагностических: один Haiku T1 с увеличенным output, четыре GLM T2 history/reset, две пятизадачные Luna-проверки инструкции памяти. Всего 59 завершённых + 1 censored в исправленной изоляции. Старый технически невалидный пилот не включён.

2. Кейс «история навредила»: GLM

В первой W1 ICL-ветка ошибается примерно так:

SELECT COUNT(*) AS operations, SUM(natt) AS attempts
FROM operations o
JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id = o.operation_id;

После join одна операция представлена несколькими строками: COUNT считает попытки, а SUM(natt) ещё раз размножает их число. Возникновение ошибки в первой задаче не вызвано межзадачной памятью. Проверяемый эффект истории — перенос её в W2, T1, T2.

В T1 стандартизованная разница получается +1,75 вместо +3 п.п.; направление эффекта всё же распознано. В T2:

sync-south Истина / fresh denominator ICL с этой историей
Операций до → во время 1000 → 1000 1150 → 1550
Терминальных отказов 25 → 175 25 → 175
Доля отказов 2,5% → 17,5% 2,17% → 11,29%
Рост 15 п.п. 9,12 п.п.

Дальше агент обсуждает якобы выросший объём трафика как альтернативное объяснение очереди. На деле выросло число повторных попыток, не бизнес-операций.

Два дополнительных history-запуска стартовали из точного pre-T2 native checkpoint; два fresh — без истории. БД и вопрос те же, никаких hints/gold/corrected SQL:

Условие Исходный Replay 1 Replay 2
Прежняя история Плохой denominator Плохой denominator Плохой denominator
Пустой контекст Верный denominator Верный denominator Верный denominator

Не путать с 3/3 полностью правильных fresh-ответа: исходный fresh имеет ошибки retries/queue timing. Оба дополнительных fresh-повтора имеют верные проверяемые числа. Это сильное свидетельство переноса конкретного ошибочного шаблона, но reset удаляет всю историю, а не единственную плохую строку. Кейc выбран после наблюдения; три реализации не дают population-оценки или статистической значимости.

Полные исходные логи: main ICL T2, history replay 1. Для остальных сохранены команды, tool-only replays и выписка шести результатов. Последняя явно помечена как восстановленная из предаварийных наблюдений, не оригинальный log.

3. Другие расхождения: не выдаём их за причинность

Модель / исходный режим T1 T2 T3
Luna fresh Числа верны Неверная telemetry Числа верны, дефект финального JSON
Luna ICL Неверный workload mix; среда повлияла Числа верны Числа верны
Luna optional managed Числа верны, слишком широкое SQL-окно Числа верны Числа верны, строка grain отличается
Haiku fresh Output censored; отдельный repeat верен Числа верны Перепутаны reference/incident
Haiku ICL Числа верны Числа верны Числа верны
Haiku optional managed Числа верны Числа верны после дорогого SQL Числа верны
GLM fresh Числа верны Denominator верен; retries/timing ошибочны Один процент противоречит counts
GLM ICL Ошибочный grain / размер эффекта Ошибочный grain / denominator Числа верны
GLM optional managed Числа верны Числа верны Числа верны, заметки прочитаны

Таблица описывает численные результаты, не полный pass по формату/SQL/интерпретации. Fresh Haiku T2/T3 выполнены в separately named continuation после остановки T1. Диагностики не подменяют исходные клетки.

Примеры механизмов:

  • Luna fresh T2 усреднила telemetry сразу за два часа и перенесла 10 workers / queue 92 в оба периода вместо 16→4 и 4→180. ICL считает раздельно. Возможная польза рабочего шаблона, но один контраст её не доказывает.
  • Haiku fresh T3 назвала предикат reference-окна is_incident, затем развернула направление тренда. Это не неспособность обнаружить новую схему.
  • GLM fresh T3 получила верные counts, но написала 3% вместо 10,5% в финале.
  • Luna ICL T1 не смогла выполнить запрос сначала из-за отсутствующего /dev/fd в минимальном chroot, затем из-за синтаксиса SQL. Ошибка финального workload mix здесь environment-affected, не чистый эффект памяти.
  • Luna managed W2 без каких-либо заметок спутала метрики и написала +65,5 вместо +18,5 п.п. Называть это вредом памяти нельзя: содержательной памяти не было.

4. Файловая память и устаревание

Исходная инструкция только сообщает, что persistent directory доступен. Luna/Haiku за пять задач ничего не записывают. GLM после W2 сохраняет answer.json (~9900 символов), не читает на T1/T2, но читает на T3. Затем пишет Markdown:

Old memory (deadline change) was a different service (parcel-index) — do not reuse.

Это наблюдаемый пример правильного ограничения применимости нерелевантного опыта. Старый JSON не удалён: добавлена заметка. Без абляции не знаем, помогло ли чтение или только добавило расходы. Полный T3 managed GLM.

Отдельные проверки инструкции, не primary

  • Даже явное объяснение fresh conversations / only memory persists не вызвало записи у Luna.
  • Общая инструкция «в начале просматривай свои заметки, перед ответом поддерживай их» вызвала чтение и перезапись notes.txt. Содержание/структуру/удаление выбирает агент, не harness.
  • Размеры после W1/W2/T1/T2/T3: 226 / 226 / 369 / 369 / 751 символ. На T1 старые сведения заменены; на T3 прочитано устаревшее active attempt_events, затем схема перепроверена и файл заменён историческими интервалами v1/v2.

Это не история сплошного успеха: maintain-вариант T2 записал незавершённый Python-скрипт и выдал пустые массивы/assessment. Lifecycle-only T3 ошибочно отнёс reference-окно к старому feed и вывел нулевые placeholders. Причинной связи этих сбоев с записанными заметками не установлено. Сохранились точные команды и размеры памяти, не полные диалоги этих двух диагностических серий.

В основных ICL T3 все модели нашли новый источник. Haiku сначала получила пустой результат старого запроса, затем исправилась. Миграция обнаружима через registry и отсутствие старых данных для новых окон; это не самый сложный случай тихого изменения семантики при правдоподобном результате. Фонового dreaming здесь нет: актуализация происходит через свежие наблюдения при очередном задании.

5. Затраты

Сумма input — по всем ходам, с повторной передачей контекста; cached — подмножество. Shell invocation может содержать несколько SQL. Wall включает сеть/серверную вариабельность.

T2 Shell Input Cached input USD Wall
Luna fresh 7 24 707 0 неизвестно 70,5 с
Luna ICL 4 87 423 23 680 неизвестно 56,9 с
Haiku fresh 10 118 259 90 892 $0,01271 66,8 с
Haiku ICL 2 144 242 132 410 $0,00646 27,3 с
GLM fresh 8 45 048 39 168 $0,00202 139,9 с
GLM ICL 4 130 926 110 592 $0,00683 23,6 с

Для Haiku это пара совпадающих по проверяемым числам правильных ответов. У Luna/GLM ответы различаются; это не цена одинакового качества.

Fresh заново читает README/schema/справочники и конструирует SQL. Haiku ICL T2 сразу переходит к предметным запросам. Но цена чтения истории способна перевесить экономию действий: GLM ICL — в ~3,4 раза дороже fresh при половине shell-вызовов. У Haiku кэш и сокращение output делают ICL дешевле.

На T3 Luna с реально поддерживаемой памятью: 8 shell / 32 044 input / 0 cached; ICL 4 / 109 585 / 53 504, fresh 10 / 33 172 / 4 480. Малый файл не устранил разведку, но не создал большого контекста. Это разные одиночные траектории и изменённая инструкция, не чистая оценка формата.

Не всю разницу input называем «лишней памятью»: меняются длины решений, часть истории полезна. В аудите раздельно prep W1/W2, target, first-target input, cache write/read, output, reasoning и эвристические категории действий. Смешанные команды не позволяют точно распределить модельные токены по «разведке»/«анализу».

SQL >1 секунды

В покрытой CLI-части четыре invocation: 56,94 с (Haiku managed T2, процесс завершён сигналом), исправленный запрос 3,05 с, 47,31 с (Haiku diagnostic T1, завершение с ошибкой), 5,90 с (Luna lifecycle W1). Большинство остальных CLI-вызовов — доли секунды. Python sqlite3 не имеет полного отдельного таймера; для него сохранён wall всего shell. Поэтому это не исчерпывающий список всех SQL >1s.

Общие расходы

  • Anthropic ledger $0,149116, плюс $0,000313 известных probes: ≈$0,14943. Включён $0,005561 за обрезанный ответ. Оценка по зафиксированным тарифам, не invoice.
  • OpenRouter ledger $0,096286, плюс $0,000052 известных probes: ≈$0,09634, источник usage.cost.
  • Codex: денежная стоимость неизвестна, подписочный доступ, не $0.

Для некоторых ранних auth/catalog/error probes per-call usage нет; полного invoice из артефактов не восстановить. Бюджеты $20/$5 не приближены. Аудит до сбоя сверил 500 успешных turns без расхождений ledger/usage/цен и восстановил 48 803 Haiku thinking tokens, потерянных только в поле нормализованной аналитики.

6. Валидность и ограничения

  1. Первая Luna-серия имела общий host /tmp; агент прочитал чужой скрипт. Вся серия invalid, сохранена отдельно. Исправлено полноценными отдельными chroot; все три Luna-ветки повторены. У исправленных 60 попыток DB hashes не менялись.
  2. Исходный grader требует буквальных period labels, хотя schema лишь string. До сбоя выполнена отдельная нормализация однозначных алиасов без исправления чисел; strict grades сохранены. Полный файл этой поздней semantic-проверки утрачен. Низкие сырые fractions нельзя читать как accuracy. Числа таблицы выше проверялись с учётом этой проблемы.
  3. Numeric pass не равен правильному SQL: слишком широкое окно может случайно совпасть на sparse snapshot; исполнимый evidence SQL может не подтверждать ответ; возможен невалидный хвост JSON.
  4. Haiku fresh T1 упёрлась в output=8192; отдельный diagnostic с 32768 завершился с верными числами. Не считаем исходную остановку аналитическим провалом памяти.
  5. Клиент сохранял/отправлял Anthropic thinking/signatures, GLM reasoning/details, Codex encrypted reasoning. Сохранённый аудит подтверждает prefix/reconstruction/payload checks, но не серверное использование состояния. Приватные checkpoints утрачены. Haiku использовала adaptive thinking с API-default effort; explicit medium не отправлялся. GLM/Luna medium.
  6. Реальные cache misses сохранены, reasoning вручную не вырезалось. Параллельность и возможный provider-wide cache не дают cold-cache причинного сравнения времени/стоимости.
  7. Одна маленькая синтетическая последовательность, постфактум выбранные diagnostics, без независимой test выборки. Нет долгосрочного накопления огромного объёма памяти. Нельзя выводить средний эффект памяти, superiority моделей или решение проблемы устаревания вообще.

Следующая содержательная проверка, пока не выполненная: старый SQL, который успешно исполняется и даёт правдоподобный, но уже неверный результат; много похожих старых инцидентов; абляция конкретного шаблона с sham-контролем; фоновые периоды в БД, чтобы неправильный фильтр времени не проходил случайно.

Сохранность результатов и восстановление после сбоя

При финальной публикации инструмент сообщил, что не смог остановить зависшую команду селективно и уничтожил весь контейнер. Перед этим Chromium-проверка HTML завершилась с кодом 137; связь с нехваткой памяти правдоподобна, точная причина сбоя не доказана. Все model runs и основной анализ к тому моменту закончились.

Последний подтверждённый удалённый commit до сбоя: 98665481f96531953c4bfb414ab70dd9a3d3da74 (15:53:43 UTC). Финальный push не состоялся. Восстановлены этот commit и отдельно выгруженный до сбоя cost_audit_bundle.zip.

Что сохранилось

  • 45 полных валидных trace.json, из них 43 основных и 2 diagnostics. SHA-256 каждого совпал с pre-crash source inventory в cost_summary.json. Ни один не пересоздан из пересказа.
  • Полный агрегированный cost/token/timing audit всех 60 попыток; все 448 оригинальных shell-команд, их SHA-256, исходные exit codes и timing. Архив аудита содержит ранее выполненную сверку 500 успешных model turns и native-history checks.
  • Генератор, seed/config, gold/reference SQL и код стенда. Обе БД повторно сгенерированы с точными первоначальными хешами.
  • Последняя версия run_study.py восстановлена из зафиксированных в разговоре правок и совпала с pre-crash SHA 5bb2e53a168d3e05e7e2f56d7acc39423ec8232182638034220886b6769cfd48. Конфигурация также совпала: d6d3bfd410e62cfcdf02f2e55f63bc8f64ffcfc0c57ea09bfb564674b03f995a.

Чего нет

Полных исходных traces нет для:

  • main-glm-stateless: T2, T3;
  • diag-glm-t2-history-r2, diag-glm-t2-reset-r1, diag-glm-t2-reset-r2: T2;
  • diag-luna-managed-lifecycle: все 5;
  • diag-luna-managed-maintain: все 5.

Также утрачены приватные native checkpoints, полный исходный per-call ledger и поздние файлы semantic-grader/подробных качественных аудитов, не успевшие попасть в GitHub. Расходы и результаты проверок ledger сохранены в предварительно выгруженном cost audit, но не выдаются за сам исходный ledger. Сохранившиеся summary.csv/json и strict grade.json — ранний срез, не итоговая accuracy-таблица.

Числа и наблюдения потерянных задач, процитированные в REPORT.md, были прочитаны и проверены до сбоя. Там, где они перенесены из консольного анализа в новую выписку, это отмечено. Не создавались фиктивные trace.json, manifest.json или model responses.

Повторное исполнение только инструментов

Для пяти GLM-задач из списка повторены все 50 сохранённых shell-команд в новой изолированной среде, на восстановленных БД. Новых model API calls нет. Сохранены оригинальные команды/их хеши и явно новые tool outputs в public_results/recovery_tool_replays/. Все 50 exit codes совпали с исходными. Неверные 1150→1550 denominators для history и верные 1000→1000 для reset воспроизведены.

Это позволяет повторно проверить вычисления/ошибку join, но не заменяет утраченные финальные ответы модели и opaque reasoning state. Нельзя использовать новые timings этих SQL как исходную стоимость модели.

Полный машиночитаемый перечень: public_results/recovery_inventory.json; ожидаемые pre-crash hashes находятся также в public_results/cost_summary.json → snapshot.source_inventory.

БД: python bench/generate.py; аудит данных: python bench/audit.py. Для новых model runs нужны внешние credentials, root/chroot/Linux/seccomp и зависимости. Перед созданием jail: python -c 'import sandbox', затем python build_jail.py. Не ослабляйте изоляцию, если эта среда недоступна.

Старые приватные checkpoint replays теперь невозможны напрямую; новые прогоны будут новыми попытками. Старый ранний pilot-luna-* имеет отдельную причину invalidation (shared /tmp), не связанную с финальным сбоем хранения.

ops AS (SELECT lo.operation_id, att.natt, CASE WHEN lo.opened_at_ms<1778151600000 THEN 'ref' ELSE 'inc' END period,
 (SELECT ra.pool_id FROM route_assignments ra WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) pool_id,
 (SELECT pp.deadline_ms FROM route_assignments ra JOIN policy_profiles pp ON pp.profile_id=ra.profile_id WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) dl
 FROM logical_operations lo JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=lo.route_id AND sr.service_id=2 JOIN att ON att.operation_id=lo.operation_id
 WHERE lo.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1778155200000)
SELECT o.period, w.pool_code, COUNT(*) ops, SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) tf,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),4) tfpct,
 SUM(o.natt) att, SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) fa,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/SUM(o.natt),4) afpct,
 SUM(CASE WHEN o.natt>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) retr, MIN(o.dl) mindl, MAX(o.dl) maxdl,
 ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN a.queue_ms END),3) qfail,
 ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN a.execution_ms END),3) efail
FROM ops o JOIN worker_pools w ON w.pool_id=o.pool_id JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;"

WITH att AS (SELECT operation_id, COUNT(*) natt FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1),
fin AS (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) mx FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1),
ops AS (SELECT lo.operation_id, CASE WHEN lo.opened_at_ms<1778151600000 THEN 'ref' ELSE 'inc' END period, att.natt,
 (SELECT ra.pool_id FROM route_assignments ra WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) pool_id,
 (SELECT pp.deadline_ms FROM route_assignments ra JOIN policy_profiles pp ON pp.profile_id=ra.profile_id WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) dl
 FROM logical_operations lo JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=lo.route_id AND sr.service_id=2 JOIN att ON att.operation_id=lo.operation_id
 WHERE lo.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1778155200000)
SELECT o.period, w.pool_code, COUNT(*) ops, SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) tf,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),4) tfpct,
 SUM(o.natt) attempts, SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) fa,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/SUM(o.natt),4) fapct,
 SUM(CASE WHEN o.natt>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) retried, MIN(o.dl) mindl, MAX(o.dl) maxdl
FROM ops o JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN worker_pools w ON w.pool_id=o.pool_id
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;
WITH fin AS (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) mx FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1),
ops AS (SELECT lo.operation_id, CASE WHEN lo.opened_at_ms<1778151600000 THEN 'ref' ELSE 'inc' END period,
 (SELECT ra.pool_id FROM route_assignments ra WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) pool_id
 FROM logical_operations lo JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=lo.route_id AND sr.service_id=2
 WHERE lo.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1778155200000),
tfops AS (SELECT o.period, o.pool_id, a.queue_ms q, a.execution_ms ex FROM ops o JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id AND a.attempt_no=f.mx JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id WHERE fc.is_success=0)
SELECT period, pool_id, ROUND(AVG(q),4) qm, ROUND(AVG(ex),4) exm, COUNT(*) n FROM tfops GROUP BY 1,2;"

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

sqlite3 -header ../data/current.db "
WITH svc AS (SELECT route_id FROM service_routes WHERE service_id=2),
ops AS (
 SELECT lo.*, ra.pool_id, pp.deadline_ms
 FROM logical_operations lo JOIN svc ON lo.route_id=svc.route_id
 JOIN route_assignments ra ON ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND lo.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms AND lo.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms
 JOIN policy_profiles pp ON pp.profile_id=ra.profile_id
 WHERE lo.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1778155200000
),
agg AS (
 SELECT o.pool_id, CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms<1778151600000 THEN '10:00-11:00' ELSE '11:00-12:00' END period,
   COUNT(*) operations,
   SUM(CASE WHEN f.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) terminal_failures,
   SUM(CASE WHEN o.nattempts>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) retried_operations,
   SUM(f.attempts) attempts, SUM(f.failed_attempts) failed_attempts,
   MIN(o.deadline_ms) min_deadline_ms, MAX(o.deadline_ms) max_deadline_ms,
   AVG(CASE WHEN f.is_success=0 THEN f.queue_ms END) failed_terminal_queue_mean_ms,
   AVG(CASE WHEN f.is_success=0 THEN f.execution_ms END) failed_terminal_execution_mean_ms
 FROM ops o
 JOIN (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) last_no, COUNT(*) attempts, SUM(CASE WHEN c.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) failed_attempts
       FROM attempt_events a JOIN failure_codes c ON c.code_id=a.code_id GROUP BY operation_id) t ON t.operation_id=o.operation_id
 JOIN attempt_events f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id AND f.attempt_no=t.last_no
 JOIN failure_codes fcc ON fcc.code_id=f.code_id
 GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT a.period, p.pool_code, operations, terminal_failures, 100.0*terminal_failures/operations terminal_failure_pct,
 attempts, failed_attempts, 100.0*failed_attempts/attempts attempt_failure_pct, retried_operations,
 min_deadline_ms, max_deadline_ms, failed_terminal_queue_mean_ms, failed_terminal_execution_mean_ms
FROM agg a JOIN worker_pools p ON p.pool_id=a.pool_id ORDER BY 2,1;
"

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.
CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

bash

cd /work; D=../data/current.db; cat > base.sql <<'EOF'
WITH ops AS (
  SELECT o.operation_id, o.opened_at_ms, o.class_id, c.class_code, a.pool_id, p.region_id, rg.region_code, rel.build_code,
    CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms >= 1777852800000 AND o.opened_at_ms < 1777856400000 THEN 'early_2026-05-04_00-01'
         WHEN o.opened_at_ms >= 1777939200000 AND o.opened_at_ms < 1777942800000 THEN 'late_2026-05-05_00-01' END AS period
  FROM logical_operations o
  JOIN service_routes r ON r.route_id=o.route_id
  JOIN services s ON s.service_id=r.service_id AND s.service_code='parcel-index'
  JOIN route_assignments a ON a.route_id=o.route_id AND o.opened_at_ms>=a.effective_from_ms AND o.opened_at_ms<a.effective_to_ms
  JOIN releases rel ON rel.release_id=a.release_id
  JOIN worker_pools p ON p.pool_id=a.pool_id
  JOIN regions rg ON rg.region_id=p.region_id
  JOIN operation_classes c ON c.class_id=o.class_id
  WHERE o.opened_at_ms >= 1777852800000 AND o.opened_at_ms < 1777856400000
     OR o.opened_at_ms >= 1777939200000 AND o.opened_at_ms < 1777942800000
),
term AS (
  SELECT e.operation_id, fc.is_success, e.attempt_no, n.nmax
  FROM attempt_events e JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=e.code_id
  JOIN (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) nmax FROM attempt_events GROUP BY operation_id) n ON n.operation_id=e.operation_id AND e.attempt_no=n.nmax
),
base AS (
  SELECT ops.*, t.is_success, CASE WHEN t.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS tf,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attempt_events e WHERE e.operation_id=ops.operation_id) AS attempts
  FROM ops JOIN term t USING(operation_id)
)
EOF

cat >/tmp/run.py <<'PY'
import sqlite3
c=sqlite3.connect('../data/current.db')
a,b=1777716000000,1777719600000; d=1777723200000
q='''select o.operation_id,o.opened_at_ms,w.pool_code,p.deadline_ms, count(e.attempt_id),sum(1-f.is_success), max(case when e.attempt_no=(select max(attempt_no) from attempt_events where operation_id=o.operation_id) then 1-f.is_success end) from logical_operations o join service_routes r using(route_id) join services s using(service_id) join route_assignments ra on ra.route_id=o.route_id and o.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms and o.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms join worker_pools w using(pool_id) join policy_profiles p using(profile_id) join attempt_events e using(operation_id) join failure_codes f using(code_id) where s.service_code='parcel-index' and o.opened_at_ms>=? and o.opened_at_ms<? group by o.operation_id'''
rows=c.execute(q,(a,d)).fetchall()
for period,lo,hi in [('reference',a,b),('incident',b,d)]:
 for pool in ['idx-north','idx-south']:
  x=[r for r in rows if lo<=r[1]<hi and r[2]==pool]
  if x:
   ops=len(x); att=sum(r[4] for r in x); fa=sum(r[5] for r in x); tf=sum(r[6] for r in x)
   print(period,pool,ops,tf,tf*100/ops,att,fa,fa*100/att,sum(r[4]>1 for r in x),min(r[3] for r in x),max(r[3] for r in x))
# telemetry
for period,lo,hi in [('reference',a,b),('incident',b,d)]:
 print(period,c.execute('select w.pool_code,t.signal_code,avg(value),t.unit from telemetry_samples x join worker_pools w using(pool_id) join telemetry_signals t using(signal_id) where measured_at_ms>=? and measured_at_ms<? and w.pool_code in ("idx-north","idx-south") group by pool_id,signal_id',(lo,hi)).fetchall())
PY

WITH base AS (
 SELECT 'reference' period,o.operation_id,o.opened_at_ms,
        ra.pool_id, oe.final_code_id, oe.attempt_count, oe.completed_at_ms
 FROM logical_operations o JOIN service_routes r ON r.route_id=o.route_id JOIN services s ON s.service_id=r.service_id
 JOIN route_assignments ra ON ra.route_id=o.route_id AND o.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms AND o.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms
 JOIN outcome_events oe ON oe.operation_id=o.operation_id
 WHERE s.service_code='ledger-sync' AND o.opened_at_ms>=1778320800000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1778324400000
 UNION ALL
 SELECT 'incident',o.operation_id,o.opened_at_ms,ec.pool_id,oe.final_code_id,oe.attempt_count,oe.completed_at_ms

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

For 2026-05-01 10:00–11:00, report total logical operations, attempts, failed attempts, terminal failures, and retried operations across all services. Then report those same five counts for each service, plus its terminal-failure percentage and the number of distinct serving physical pools represented in the window. Explain briefly in caveats why attempts and terminal failures are not interchangeable. This is a counting calibration, not an incident attribution exercise.

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.
CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

WITH att AS (SELECT operation_id, COUNT(*) natt, MAX(CASE WHEN attempt_no=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) dummy FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1),
ops AS (
 SELECT lo.operation_id, sr.service_id, a.natt,
  (SELECT ra.pool_id FROM route_assignments ra WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) AS pool_id
 FROM logical_operations lo JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=lo.route_id
 LEFT JOIN att a ON a.operation_id=lo.operation_id
 WHERE lo.opened_at_ms>=1777629600000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1777633200000),
fin AS (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) mx FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1)
SELECT s.service_code,
 COUNT(*) operations, SUM(o.natt) attempts,
 SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) failed_attempts,
 SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) terminal_failures,
 SUM(CASE WHEN o.natt>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) retried,
 COUNT(DISTINCT o.pool_id) physical_pools
FROM ops o JOIN services s USING(service_id) JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id
GROUP BY 1 UNION ALL
SELECT 'TOTAL',COUNT(*),SUM(natt),SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),
 SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),
 SUM(CASE WHEN natt>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),COUNT(DISTINCT pool_id)
FROM ops o JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id;"

Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Investigate parcel-index on 2026-05-02, comparing reference 10:00–11:00 with incident 11:00–12:00. For every period and serving physical pool, report operations, terminal failures and their percentage, attempts, failed attempts and their percentage, retried operations, and minimum/maximum applied deadline_ms. Report ordinary window means of every recorded telemetry signal for those pools, and applied changes during 10:00–12:00 (kind, pool, effective time, before/after JSON strings). In assessment, identify the most strongly supported proximal explanation, the affected pool and the terminal-failure increase in percentage points; contrast it with at least one plausible alternative. Distinguish evidence from causal proof. Attribute configuration at the time the operation entered the system, not from today's configuration.

    "WITH att AS (SELECT operation_id, COUNT(*) natt FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1), fin AS (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) mx FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1), ops AS (SELECT lo.operation_id, CASE WHEN lo.opened_at_ms<1777719600000 THEN 'ref' ELSE 'inc' END period, att.natt, (SELECT ra.pool_id FROM route_assignments ra WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) pool_id, (SELECT pp.deadline_ms FROM route_assignments ra JOIN policy_profiles pp ON pp.profile_id=ra.profile_id WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) dl FROM logical_operations lo JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=lo.route_id AND sr.service_id=1 JOIN att ON att.operation_id=lo.operation_id WHERE lo.opened_at_ms>=1777716000000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1777723200000) SELECT o.period, w.pool_code, COUNT(*) operations, SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) terminal_failures, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),4) terminal_failure_pct, SUM(o.natt) attempts, SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) failed_attempts, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/SUM(o.natt),4) attempt_failure_pct, SUM(CASE WHEN o.natt>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) retried_operations, MIN(o.dl) min_deadline_ms, MAX(o.dl) max_deadline_ms FROM ops o JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN worker_pools w ON w.pool_id=o.pool_id GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;",
    "SELECT w.pool_code, s.signal_code, s.unit, CASE WHEN ts.measured_at_ms<1777719600000 THEN 'ref' ELSE 'inc' END period, AVG(ts.value) mean_value, COUNT(*) samples FROM telemetry_samples ts JOIN worker_pools w ON w.pool_id=ts.pool_id JOIN telemetry_signals s ON s.signal_id=ts.signal_id WHERE ts.pool_id IN (1,2) AND ts.measured_at_ms>=1777716000000 AND ts.measured_at_ms<1777723200000 GROUP BY 4,1,2 ORDER BY 4,1,2;",
    "SELECT ra.route_id, ra.effective_from_ms, ra.effective_to_ms, ra.pool_id, ra.profile_id, p.deadline_ms FROM route_assignments ra JOIN policy_profiles p ON p.profile_id=ra.profile_id WHERE ra.pool_id IN (1,2) ORDER BY ra.route_id, ra.effective_from_ms;"
  ]
}

Ход 3 · model 3.22 s
bash
D=/data/current.db; sqlite3 -header -column $D "
WITH att AS (SELECT operation_id, COUNT(*) natt FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1),
fin AS (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) mx FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1),
asg AS (SELECT lo.opened_at_ms t, lo.route_id, lo.operation_id, lo.class_id),
ops AS (SELECT lo.operation_id, lo.class_id, lo.opened_at_ms, att.natt,
 CASE WHEN lo.opened_at_ms<1777856400000 THEN 'early' ELSE 'late' END period,
 (SELECT ra.release_id FROM route_assignments ra WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) rel,
 (SELECT ra.pool_id FROM route_assignments ra WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) pool_id
 FROM logical_operations lo JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=lo.route_id AND sr.service_id=1 JOIN att ON att.operation_id=lo.operation_id
 WHERE (lo.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1777856400000) OR (lo.opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1777942800000))
SELECT o.period, r.region_code, c.class_code, rel.build_code, COUNT(*) ops,
 SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) tf,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),4) pct
FROM ops o JOIN worker_pools w ON w.pool_id=o.pool_id JOIN regions r ON r.region_id=w.region_id JOIN operation_classes c ON c.class_id=o.class_id JOIN releases rel ON rel.release_id=o.rel
JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 1,2,3,4;"

D=/data/current.db; sqlite3 -header -column $D "
WITH ops AS (SELECT lo.operation_id, lo.class_id, CASE WHEN lo.opened_at_ms<1777856400000 THEN 'early' ELSE 'late' END period
 FROM logical_operations lo JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=lo.route_id AND sr.service_id=1
 WHERE (lo.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1777856400000) OR (lo.opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1777942800000)),
fin AS (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) mx FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1)
SELECT period, c.class_code, COUNT(*) ops, ROUND(100.0*COUNT(*)/SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY period),4) share,
 SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) tf,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),4) pct
FROM ops o JOIN operation_classes c ON c.class_id=o.class_id
JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id
GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;

 FROM logical_operations lo JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=lo.route_id AND sr.service_id=1
 WHERE (lo.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1777856400000) OR (lo.opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1777942800000)),
fin AS (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) mx FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1)
SELECT rel.build_code, COUNT(*) ops, SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) tf,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),4) pct
FROM ops o JOIN releases rel ON rel.release_id=o.rel JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id
GROUP BY 1;"

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Investigate ledger-sync on 2026-05-07, reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. For every period and serving physical pool report operations, terminal failures and percentage, attempts, failed attempts and percentage, retried operations, minimum/maximum applied deadline_ms, and mean queue_ms and execution_ms of the terminal attempt among terminally failed operations. Report means of every recorded telemetry signal for those pools and applied changes during 10:00–12:00 (kind, pool, effective time, before/after JSON strings). In assessment identify the strongest supported proximal explanation, the affected pool and failure increase in pp. Explicitly evaluate both a deadline-policy change and worker/queue pressure against the current evidence. Explain the remaining causal limitation.

    "assessment": "Strongest supported proximal explanation: a worker-limit (worker concurrency) reduction on sync-south effective at 1778151600000 (exactly 11:00 UTC, the incident start) from 16 to 4 workers. The affected pool is sync-south, where terminal failures rose from 2.17% to 11.29% (+9.12 percentage points; attempts-failure 11.67% -> 24.17%), with synchronously degraded measurements: mean queue_depth 4 -> 180 operations, mean available_workers 16 -> 4, and mean per-attempt queue_ms of terminally failed attempts rising from 5 ms to 235 ms while their execution_ms collapsed to 15 ms, indicating operations waiting almost the entire 250 ms budget in queue and dying to deadline exhaustion. Deadlines were evaluated at operation-open time from route_assignments and were 250 ms for every operation on every pool in both periods, so the deadline-policy-change hypothesis is REFUTED by the evidence: no deadline_policy change_event exists for service 2 in this window, and min=max=250 ms throughout. Incoming volume barely moved (1150 -> 1550 operations on sync-south), insufficient to explain a 45x queue-depth increase, whereas a 16->4 worker cap mechanically produces it. Telemetry on sync-north was identical across periods (baseline control). Causal limitation: this remains observational. The temporal coincidence, exclusivity to the affected pool and mechanistic coherence (fewer workers -> longer queueing -> deadline misses) make the worker-limit change the best-supported proximal candidate, but we cannot exclude an unmeasured confounder acting simultaneously on sync-south, and applied configuration describes what changed, not a controlled experiment that isolates its isolated effect; association and mechanism-support, not proof, is what these data establish."

    "Terminal-failure percentages use logical operations as denominator; attempt-failure percentages use attempts; failed-then-recovered attempts are not terminal failures.",
    "failed_terminal_queue_mean_ms / failed_terminal_execution_mean_ms are means over the final attempt of terminally failed operations only (per-attempt times exclude retry backoff).",

    "WITH att AS (SELECT operation_id, COUNT(*) natt FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1), fin AS (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) mx FROM attempt_events GROUP BY 1), ops AS (SELECT lo.operation_id, CASE WHEN lo.opened_at_ms<1778151600000 THEN 'ref' ELSE 'inc' END period, att.natt, (SELECT ra.pool_id FROM route_assignments ra WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) pool_id, (SELECT pp.deadline_ms FROM route_assignments ra JOIN policy_profiles pp ON pp.profile_id=ra.profile_id WHERE ra.route_id=lo.route_id AND ra.effective_from_ms<=lo.opened_at_ms AND ra.effective_to_ms>lo.opened_at_ms) dl FROM logical_operations lo JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=lo.route_id AND sr.service_id=2 JOIN att ON att.operation_id=lo.operation_id WHERE lo.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 AND lo.opened_at_ms<1778155200000) SELECT o.period, w.pool_code, COUNT(*) operations, SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) terminal_failures, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),4) terminal_failure_pct, SUM(o.natt) attempts, SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) failed_attempts, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/SUM(o.natt),4) attempt_failure_pct, SUM(CASE WHEN o.natt>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) retried_operations, MIN(o.dl) min_deadline_ms, MAX(o.dl) max_deadline_ms, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN a.queue_ms END),4) failed_terminal_queue_mean_ms, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN fc.is_success=0 AND a.attempt_no=f.mx THEN a.execution_ms END),4) failed_terminal_execution_mean_ms FROM ops o JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN fin f ON f.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN worker_pools w ON w.pool_id=o.pool_id GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2;",
    "SELECT w.pool_code, s.signal_code, s.unit, CASE WHEN ts.measured_at_ms<1778151600000 THEN 'ref' ELSE 'inc' END period, AVG(ts.value) mean_value, COUNT(*) samples FROM telemetry_samples ts JOIN worker_pools w ON w.pool_id=ts.pool_id JOIN telemetry_signals s ON s.signal_id=ts.signal_id WHERE ts.pool_id IN (3,4) AND ts.measured_at_ms>=1778148000000 AND ts.measured_at_ms<1778155200000 GROUP BY 4,1,2 ORDER BY 4,1,2;",
    "SELECT ra.route_id, ra.effective_from_ms, ra.effective_to_ms, ra.pool_id, p.deadline_ms FROM route_assignments ra JOIN policy_profiles p ON p.profile_id=ra.profile_id WHERE ra.pool_id IN (3,4) ORDER BY ra.route_id, ra.effective_from_ms;",

Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Report ledger-sync reliability for 2026-05-09: reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. Report the authoritative event source for these windows (registry version, event table, event grain and effective start). For each period and actual serving PHYSICAL pool, report logical operations, terminal failures, terminal-failure percentage, retried operations, retry percentage and mean end-to-end latency_ms. Do not treat routing intent or an individual execution identity as a physical pool. Also give all-pool operations, terminal failures and terminal-failure percentage per period; identify the physical pool with the largest increase and report that increase in pp. In assessment state what the report establishes and the important attribution/counting limitations.

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

For 2026-05-01 10:00–11:00, report total logical operations, attempts, failed attempts, terminal failures, and retried operations across all services. Then report those same five counts for each service, plus its terminal-failure percentage and the number of distinct serving physical pools represented in the window. Explain briefly in caveats why attempts and terminal failures are not interchangeable. This is a counting calibration, not an incident attribution exercise.
