# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.
current.db
CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

SELECT period, pool, COUNT(*) ops, SUM(CASE WHEN ok.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) tf,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN ok.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),4) tfp,
 COUNT(a2.attempt_id) att, SUM(CASE WHEN a2.code_id=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) fa,
 ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN a2.code_id=2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(a2.attempt_id),4) afp,
 SUM(CASE WHEN att.n>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) retried,
 MIN(ap.deadline_ms), MAX(ap.deadline_ms)
FROM ops o
JOIN (SELECT operation_id, MAX(attempt_no) mx, COUNT(*) n FROM attempt_events GROUP BY operation_id) att ON att.operation_id=o.operation_id
JOIN attempt_events a2 ON a2.operation_id=o.operation_id AND a2.attempt_no=att.mx
JOIN failure_codes ok ON ok.code_id=a2.code_id
JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=(SELECT route_id FROM logical_operations WHERE operation_id=o.operation_id)
JOIN route_assignments ra ON ra.route_id=sr.route_id AND (SELECT opened_at_ms FROM logical_operations WHERE operation_id=o.operation_id)>=ra.effective_from_ms AND (SELECT opened_at_ms FROM logical_operations WHERE operation_id=o.operation_id)<ra.effective_to_ms
JOIN policy_profiles ap ON ap.profile_id=ra.profile_id
GROUP BY period, pool;"

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));

CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE TABLE outcome_events(outcome_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES logical_operations, cell_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES execution_cells, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, final_code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, attempt_count INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_count>=1), total_queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(total_queue_ms>=0), total_execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(total_execution_ms>=0), total_backoff_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(total_backoff_ms>=0));
CREATE INDEX outcomes_cell ON outcome_events(cell_id,operation_id);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);

A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Then report those same five counts for each service, plus its terminal-failure percentage and the number of distinct serving physical pools represented in the window. Explain briefly in caveats why attempts and terminal failures are not interchangeable. This is a counting calibration, not an incident attribution exercise.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

  from logical_operations o join service_routes r using(route_id) where r.service_id=(select service_id from services where service_code='parcel-index') and o.opened_at_ms>=1777716000000 and o.opened_at_ms<1777723200000),
asg as (select ops.*, ra.pool_id, ra.profile_id, ra.release_id, ra.assignment_id from ops join route_assignments ra on ra.route_id=ops.route_id and ops.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms and ops.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms),
att as (select a.operation_id, count(*) n, sum(f.is_success=0) failed from attempt_events a join failure_codes f using(code_id) group by a.operation_id),
lst as (select a.operation_id, f.is_success last_ok from attempt_events a join failure_codes f using(code_id) where a.attempt_no=(select max(b.attempt_no) from attempt_events b where b.operation_id=a.operation_id))
select asg.period, p.pool_code, count(*) operations, sum(lst.last_ok=0) terminal_failures, round(100.0*sum(lst.last_ok=0)/count(*),4) terminal_pct,
 sum(att.n) attempts, sum(att.failed) failed_attempts, round(100.0*sum(att.failed)/sum(att.n),4) attempt_pct, sum(att.n>1) retried, min(d.deadline_ms) min_deadline, max(d.deadline_ms) max_deadline
from asg join worker_pools p using(pool_id) join policy_profiles d on d.profile_id=asg.profile_id join att using(operation_id) join lst using(operation_id)
where asg.period is not null group by asg.period, p.pool_code order by 1,2;
EOF

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Evaluate parcel-index during early 2026-05-04 00:00–01:00 and late 2026-05-05 00:00–01:00. Candidate build is idx-r19 and reference is idx-r18. (1) For each period report operations, terminal failures, failure percentage, and candidate traffic percentage. (2) Pool both periods and report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage per build. (3) Report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage for each period × region × operation-class × build cell. These define eight matched slices (period × region × operation class), each containing both builds. (4) Standardize each build by giving those eight slices equal weight; report both standardized failure percentages, candidate minus reference in pp, and the number of slices where candidate is worse. (5) Report period × operation-class traffic shares and failure percentages. In assessment, explain whether the time trend and pooled build comparison support the claim “expanding the candidate improved reliability.” Identify the strongest measured association and distinguish a possible root-cause hypothesis from causal identification. Do not extrapolate beyond the observed strata. Equal weighting here is the specified target population, not weighting by observed build traffic.

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Investigate ledger-sync on 2026-05-07, reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. For every period and serving physical pool report operations, terminal failures and percentage, attempts, failed attempts and percentage, retried operations, minimum/maximum applied deadline_ms, and mean queue_ms and execution_ms of the terminal attempt among terminally failed operations. Report means of every recorded telemetry signal for those pools and applied changes during 10:00–12:00 (kind, pool, effective time, before/after JSON strings). In assessment identify the strongest supported proximal explanation, the affected pool and failure increase in pp. Explicitly evaluate both a deadline-policy change and worker/queue pressure against the current evidence. Explain the remaining causal limitation.

with ops as (select o.operation_id, o.route_id, o.opened_at_ms, case when o.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778151600000 then 'reference_10_11' when o.opened_at_ms>=1778151600000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778155200000 then 'incident_11_12' end period
 from logical_operations o join service_routes r using(route_id) join services s on s.service_id=r.service_id where s.service_code='ledger-sync' and o.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778155200000),
asg as (select ops.*, ra.pool_id, ra.profile_id from ops join route_assignments ra on ra.route_id=ops.route_id and ops.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms and ops.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms),
att as (select a.operation_id, count(*) n, sum(f.is_success=0) failed from attempt_events a join failure_codes f using(code_id) group by a.operation_id),
lst as (select a.operation_id, f.is_success last_ok, a.queue_ms, a.execution_ms from attempt_events a join failure_codes f using(code_id) where a.attempt_no=(select max(b.attempt_no) from attempt_events b where b.operation_id=a.operation_id))
select asg.period, p.pool_code, count(*) operations, sum(lst.last_ok=0) terminal_failures, round(100.0*sum(lst.last_ok=0)/count(*),4) terminal_failure_pct,
 sum(att.n) attempts, sum(att.failed) failed_attempts, round(100.0*sum(att.failed)/sum(att.n),4) attempt_failure_pct, sum(att.n>1) retried_operations,
 min(d.deadline_ms) min_deadline_ms, max(d.deadline_ms) max_deadline_ms,
 round(avg(case when lst.last_ok=0 then lst.queue_ms end),4) failed_terminal_queue_mean_ms, round(avg(case when lst.last_ok=0 then lst.execution_ms end),4) failed_terminal_execution_mean_ms
from asg join worker_pools p using(pool_id) join policy_profiles d on d.profile_id=asg.profile_id join att using(operation_id) join lst using(operation_id) where asg.period is not null group by asg.period, p.pool_code order by 1,2;

Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Report ledger-sync reliability for 2026-05-09: reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. Report the authoritative event source for these windows (registry version, event table, event grain and effective start). For each period and actual serving PHYSICAL pool, report logical operations, terminal failures, terminal-failure percentage, retried operations, retry percentage and mean end-to-end latency_ms. Do not treat routing intent or an individual execution identity as a physical pool. Also give all-pool operations, terminal failures and terminal-failure percentage per period; identify the physical pool with the largest increase and report that increase in pp. In assessment state what the report establishes and the important attribution/counting limitations.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Investigate parcel-index on 2026-05-02, comparing reference 10:00–11:00 with incident 11:00–12:00. For every period and serving physical pool, report operations, terminal failures and their percentage, attempts, failed attempts and their percentage, retried operations, and minimum/maximum applied deadline_ms. Report ordinary window means of every recorded telemetry signal for those pools, and applied changes during 10:00–12:00 (kind, pool, effective time, before/after JSON strings). In assessment, identify the most strongly supported proximal explanation, the affected pool and the terminal-failure increase in percentage points; contrast it with at least one plausible alternative. Distinguish evidence from causal proof. Attribute configuration at the time the operation entered the system, not from today's configuration.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

Ход 6 · model 9.15 s
bash
cd ..; cat > work/q1.sql <<'EOF'
WITH ops AS (
  SELECT o.operation_id, o.route_id, o.opened_at_ms,
    CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms>=1777716000000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777719600000 THEN 'reference_10_11'
         WHEN o.opened_at_ms>=1777719600000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777723200000 THEN 'incident_11_12' END AS period
  FROM logical_operations o JOIN service_routes r ON r.route_id=o.route_id
  WHERE r.service_id=1 AND o.opened_at_ms>=1777716000000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777723200000
),
asg AS (
  SELECT ops.*, a.pool_id, a.profile_id, a.release_id, a.assignment_id
  FROM ops JOIN route_assignments a ON a.route_id=ops.route_id
   AND ops.opened_at_ms>=a.effective_from_ms AND ops.opened_at_ms<a.effective_to_ms
),
att AS (
  SELECT asg.*, e.attempt_no, e.attempt_id, fc.is_success, p.deadline_ms,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY asg.operation_id ORDER BY e.attempt_no DESC) rn,
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY asg.operation_id) n_att
  FROM asg JOIN attempt_events e ON e.operation_id=asg.operation_id
  JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=e.code_id
  JOIN policy_profiles p ON p.profile_id=asg.profile_id
)
SELECT period, pool_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT operation_id) ops,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN rn=1 AND is_success=0 THEN operation_id END) terminal_failures,
  COUNT(*) attempts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) failed_attempts,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN n_att>1 THEN operation_id END) retried_ops,
  MIN(deadline_ms) min_dl, MAX(deadline_ms) max_dl
FROM att GROUP BY period, pool_id ORDER BY period, pool_id;
EOF

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

bash
cd ../data && cat > /tmp/base.sql <<'EOF'
WITH ops AS (
  SELECT o.operation_id, o.opened_at_ms, o.route_id, oc.class_code, r.region_code, rel.build_code,
         (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM route_assignments ra WHERE ra.route_id=o.route_id AND o.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms AND o.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms) AS n_asg
  FROM logical_operations o
  JOIN operation_classes oc ON oc.class_id=o.class_id
  JOIN route_assignments ra ON ra.route_id=o.route_id AND o.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms AND o.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms
  JOIN worker_pools wp ON wp.pool_id=ra.pool_id
  JOIN regions r ON r.region_id=wp.region_id
  JOIN releases rel ON rel.release_id=ra.release_id
  WHERE o.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777856400000 OR o.opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777942800000
),
last AS (
  SELECT a.operation_id, a.code_id, fc.is_success FROM attempt_events a JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id
  WHERE a.attempt_no=(SELECT MAX(attempt_no) FROM attempt_events b WHERE b.operation_id=a.operation_id)
)
EOF
sqlite3 -header current.db "$(cat /tmp/base.sql) SELECT n_asg, count(*) FROM ops GROUP BY 1; SELECT count(*), count(l.operation_id) FROM ops LEFT JOIN last l USING(operation_id);"

{"answer":{"assessment":"Strongest supported proximal explanation: the worker concurrency limit applied to sync-south (pool sync-south, ledger-sync, 16 -> 4 workers at 2026-05-07 11:00 UTC). In the incident window sync-south available_workers fell from a 16.0 mean to 4.0, queue_depth rose from 4.0 to 180.0, and failed terminal attempts were queue-dominated (mean queue 235.0 ms vs execution 15.0 ms, against 5.0 ms queue / 245.0 ms execution in the reference window). Terminal failure rate on sync-south rose from 2.5% (25/1000) to 17.5% (175/1000), +15.0 pp; attempt failure rose from 15.2% to 46.8% (+31.6 pp). sync-north stayed at 2.5% terminal failure in both windows, and its telemetry was flat. Upstream p95 latency (118 ms) and CPU (0.42) were unchanged on sync-south, so an upstream slowdown is not supported. Deadline-policy change: not supported as the cause of the ledger-sync increase. The applied deadline for every ledger-sync operation in both windows was 250 ms (profile balanced-250); the only deadline_policy changes in the data (80 ms then restored to 250 ms) apply to parcel-index pool idx-north on 2026-05-02, outside these windows and outside ledger-sync. Worker/queue pressure is the better-supported explanation: queue depth and queue time on the failed terminal attempts moved sharply on the same pool and time the worker limit was applied, and the increase appeared across both sync-south routes (4 and 8) and both operation classes. CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

with ops as (
  select o.operation_id, o.opened_at_ms,
    case when o.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778151600000 then 'reference_10_11'
         when o.opened_at_ms>=1778151600000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778155200000 then 'incident_11_12' end period,
    p.pool_code, pp.deadline_ms
  from logical_operations o

  join route_assignments a on a.route_id=o.route_id and o.opened_at_ms>=a.effective_from_ms and o.opened_at_ms<a.effective_to_ms
  join worker_pools p on p.pool_id=a.pool_id
  join policy_profiles pp on pp.profile_id=a.profile_id
  where o.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 and o.opened_at_ms<1778155200000
),
att as (
  select ae.operation_id, ae.attempt_no, ae.queue_ms, ae.execution_ms, fc.is_success,
    count(*) over (partition by ae.operation_id) natt,
    row_number() over (partition by ae.operation_id order by ae.attempt_no desc) rn_desc
  from attempt_events ae join failure_codes fc on fc.code_id=ae.code_id
  where ae.operation_id in (select operation_id from ops)
),
opstat as (
  select ops.period, ops.pool_code, ops.deadline_ms, ops.operation_id,
    max(case when att.rn_desc=1 then att.is_success end) final_success,
    max(case when att.rn_desc=1 then att.queue_ms end) final_queue,
    max(case when att.rn_desc=1 then att.execution_ms end) final_exec,
    max(att.natt) natt,
    sum(att.is_success=0) failed_attempts
  from ops join att using(operation_id) group by 1,2,3,4
)
select period, pool_code, count(*) operations,
  sum(final_success=0) terminal_failures,
  round(100.0*sum(final_success=0)/count(*),4) terminal_failure_pct,
  sum(natt) attempts, sum(failed_attempts) failed_attempts,
  round(100.0*sum(failed_attempts)/sum(natt),4) attempt_failure_pct,
  sum(natt>1) retried_operations,
  min(deadline_ms) min_deadline_ms, max(deadline_ms) max_deadline_ms,
  round(avg(case when final_success=0 then final_queue end),4) failed_terminal_queue_mean_ms,
  round(avg(case when final_success=0 then final_exec end),4) failed_terminal_execution_mean_ms
from opstat group by period, pool_code order by period, pool_code;

assessment=("Strongest supported proximal explanation: the worker concurrency limit applied to sync-south (pool sync-south, ledger-sync, 16 -> 4 workers at 2026-05-07 11:00 UTC). "
"In the incident window sync-south available_workers fell from a 16.0 mean to 4.0, queue_depth rose from 4.0 to 180.0, and failed terminal attempts were queue-dominated (mean queue 235.0 ms vs execution 15.0 ms, against 5.0 ms queue / 245.0 ms execution in the reference window). "
"Terminal failure rate on sync-south rose from 2.5% (25/1000) to 17.5% (175/1000), +15.0 pp; attempt failure rose from 15.2% to 46.8% (+31.6 pp). sync-north stayed at 2.5% terminal failure in both windows, and its telemetry was flat. Upstream p95 latency (118 ms) and CPU (0.42) were unchanged on sync-south, so an upstream slowdown is not supported. "
"Deadline-policy change: not supported as the cause of the ledger-sync increase. The applied deadline for every ledger-sync operation in both windows was 250 ms (profile balanced-250); the only deadline_policy changes in the data (80 ms then restored to 250 ms) apply to parcel-index pool idx-north on 2026-05-02, outside these windows and outside ledger-sync. "
"Worker/queue pressure is the better-supported explanation: queue depth and queue time on the failed terminal attempts moved sharply on the same pool and time the worker limit was applied, and the increase appeared across both sync-south routes (4 and 8) and both operation classes. "
"Remaining causal limitation: this is an observational before/after comparison of one applied configuration change on one pool, with no randomized or concurrent control pool. The contrast with sync-north is supportive but not a true control (different pool, different region, and route-level pool attribution differs), and the change, traffic mix and any other concurrent change cannot be fully separated; the association is strong but causation is not proven.")
caveats=[
 "Pool attribution uses the route assignment effective at logical operation open time (feed_registry v1, routing-time attribution). Route 8 (sync-alias-s) is an alias that maps to pool sync-south, so it is not counted as a separate pool.",
 "Windows are UTC half-open by logical operation open time: reference [1778148000000,1778151600000) and incident [1778151600000,1778155200000). Each period has 1000 operations per pool.",
 "Failed-terminal queue/execution means use the final attempt of terminally failed operations only (attempt-level queue_ms and execution_ms exclude retry backoff). All terminal failures carry the DEADLINE code.",
 "Telemetry means are plain arithmetic means of the samples in each period (12 samples per signal per pool per period, about 5-minute spacing). Telemetry is sampled independently, so it is descriptive and not an operation-weighted metric.",
 "The incident-window applied change is a single configuration change (worker_limit) with no randomized assignment; treat it as an observational association.",
 "Only ledger-sync routes (3, 4, 8) were analysed; the 11:00 change is attributed to pool sync-south (pool_id 4) as recorded in change_events.",
]

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Report ledger-sync reliability for 2026-05-09: reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. Report the authoritative event source for these windows (registry version, event table, event grain and effective start). For each period and actual serving PHYSICAL pool, report logical operations, terminal failures, terminal-failure percentage, retried operations, retry percentage and mean end-to-end latency_ms. Do not treat routing intent or an individual execution identity as a physical pool. Also give all-pool operations, terminal failures and terminal-failure percentage per period; identify the physical pool with the largest increase and report that increase in pp. In assessment state what the report establishes and the important attribution/counting limitations.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE execution_cells(cell_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, cell_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE outcome_events(outcome_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES logical_operations, cell_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES execution_cells, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, final_code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, attempt_count INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_count>=1), total_queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(total_queue_ms>=0), total_execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(total_execution_ms>=0), total_backoff_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(total_backoff_ms>=0));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);
CREATE INDEX outcomes_cell ON outcome_events(cell_id,operation_id);
