# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

For 2026-05-01 10:00–11:00, report total logical operations, attempts, failed attempts, terminal failures, and retried operations across all services. Then report those same five counts for each service, plus its terminal-failure percentage and the number of distinct serving physical pools represented in the window. Explain briefly in caveats why attempts and terminal failures are not interchangeable. This is a counting calibration, not an incident attribution exercise.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Investigate parcel-index on 2026-05-02, comparing reference 10:00–11:00 with incident 11:00–12:00. For every period and serving physical pool, report operations, terminal failures and their percentage, attempts, failed attempts and their percentage, retried operations, and minimum/maximum applied deadline_ms. Report ordinary window means of every recorded telemetry signal for those pools, and applied changes during 10:00–12:00 (kind, pool, effective time, before/after JSON strings). In assessment, identify the most strongly supported proximal explanation, the affected pool and the terminal-failure increase in percentage points; contrast it with at least one plausible alternative. Distinguish evidence from causal proof. Attribute configuration at the time the operation entered the system, not from today's configuration.

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

Ход 7 · model 4.68 s
bash
cd /work; cat > ops.sql <<'EOF'
WITH ops AS (
  SELECT o.operation_id, o.opened_at_ms, r.pool_id, p.deadline_ms,
         CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms>=1777719600000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777723200000 THEN 'reference_10_11'
              WHEN o.opened_at_ms>=1777723200000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777726800000 THEN 'incident_11_12' END AS period
  FROM logical_operations o
  JOIN service_routes sr ON sr.route_id=o.route_id AND sr.service_id=1
  JOIN route_assignments r ON r.route_id=o.route_id AND o.opened_at_ms>=r.effective_from_ms AND o.opened_at_ms<r.effective_to_ms
  JOIN policy_profiles p ON p.profile_id=r.profile_id
  WHERE o.opened_at_ms>=1777719600000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777726800000
),
att AS (
  SELECT a.operation_id, COUNT(*) n, SUM(fc.is_success=0) failed,
         MAX(CASE WHEN a.attempt_no=(SELECT MAX(attempt_no) FROM attempt_events x WHERE x.operation_id=a.operation_id) THEN fc.is_success END) final_success
  FROM attempt_events a JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id GROUP BY a.operation_id
)
SELECT ops.period, wp.pool_code, COUNT(*) operations,
  SUM(att.final_success=0) terminal_failures,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(att.final_success=0)/COUNT(*),4) terminal_failure_pct,
  SUM(att.n) attempts, SUM(att.failed) failed_attempts,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(att.failed)/SUM(att.n),4) attempt_failure_pct,
  SUM(att.n>1) retried_operations, MIN(ops.deadline_ms) min_deadline_ms, MAX(ops.deadline_ms) max_deadline_ms
FROM ops JOIN att USING(operation_id) JOIN worker_pools wp ON wp.pool_id=ops.pool_id
GROUP BY ops.period, wp.pool_code ORDER BY ops.period, wp.pool_code;
EOF
sqlite3 -header /data/current.db < ops.sql

WITH ops AS (

         CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms>=1777716000000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777719600000 THEN 'reference_10_11'
              WHEN o.opened_at_ms>=1777719600000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777723200000 THEN 'incident_11_12' END AS period
  FROM logical_operations o
  JOIN route_assignments r ON r.route_id=o.route_id AND o.opened_at_ms>=r.effective_from_ms AND o.opened_at_ms<r.effective_to_ms
  JOIN policy_profiles p ON p.profile_id=r.profile_id
  WHERE o.opened_at_ms>=1777716000000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777723200000
)
SELECT ops.period, wp.pool_code, a.attempt_no, fc.code, COUNT(*) attempts,
  ROUND(AVG(a.queue_ms),1) avg_queue, ROUND(AVG(a.execution_ms),1) avg_exec, MIN(a.execution_ms), MAX(a.execution_ms)
FROM ops JOIN attempt_events a USING(operation_id) JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id JOIN worker_pools wp ON wp.pool_id=ops.pool_id
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,1,3,4;
EOF

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Evaluate parcel-index during early 2026-05-04 00:00–01:00 and late 2026-05-05 00:00–01:00. Candidate build is idx-r19 and reference is idx-r18. (1) For each period report operations, terminal failures, failure percentage, and candidate traffic percentage. (2) Pool both periods and report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage per build. (3) Report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage for each period × region × operation-class × build cell. These define eight matched slices (period × region × operation class), each containing both builds. (4) Standardize each build by giving those eight slices equal weight; report both standardized failure percentages, candidate minus reference in pp, and the number of slices where candidate is worse. (5) Report period × operation-class traffic shares and failure percentages. In assessment, explain whether the time trend and pooled build comparison support the claim “expanding the candidate improved reliability.” Identify the strongest measured association and distinguish a possible root-cause hypothesis from causal identification. Do not extrapolate beyond the observed strata. Equal weighting here is the specified target population, not weighting by observed build traffic.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

Ход 7 · model 3.77 s
bash
cd /work; D=../data/current.db; cat > base.sql <<'EOF'
WITH ops AS (
  SELECT o.operation_id, o.opened_at_ms, oc.class_code, r.build_code, rg.region_code, p.pool_code,
    CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777856400000 THEN 'early_2026-05-04_00-01'
         WHEN o.opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777942800000 THEN 'late_2026-05-05_00-01' END AS period
  FROM logical_operations o
  JOIN operation_classes oc ON oc.class_id=o.class_id
  JOIN route_assignments ra ON ra.route_id=o.route_id AND o.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms AND o.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms
  JOIN releases r ON r.release_id=ra.release_id
  JOIN worker_pools p ON p.pool_id=ra.pool_id
  JOIN regions rg ON rg.region_id=p.region_id
  WHERE (o.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777856400000) OR (o.opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777942800000)
),
last_att AS (
  SELECT a.operation_id, fc.is_success FROM attempt_events a JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=a.code_id
  WHERE a.attempt_no=(SELECT MAX(attempt_no) FROM attempt_events b WHERE b.operation_id=a.operation_id)
),
opf AS (
  SELECT ops.*, CASE WHEN la.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS tf FROM ops JOIN last_att la ON la.operation_id=ops.operation_id
)
EOF
sqlite3 -header $D "$(cat base.sql) SELECT count(*), sum(tf) FROM opf; SELECT period, build_code, count(*) n, sum(tf) f FROM opf GROUP BY 1,2;"; sqlite3 $D "select count(*) from logical_operations where opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 and opened_at_ms<1777856400000; select count(*) from logical_operations where opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 and opened_at_ms<1777942800000"

cd /work; cat > gen.py <<'EOF'
import json, sqlite3
base = open('base.sql').read()
qs = [
 base + "SELECT period, COUNT(*) AS operations, SUM(tf) AS terminal_failures, ROUND(100.0*SUM(tf)/COUNT(*),4) AS terminal_failure_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN build_code='idx-r19' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),4) AS candidate_traffic_pct FROM opf GROUP BY period ORDER BY period;",
 base + "SELECT build_code, COUNT(*) AS operations, SUM(tf) AS terminal_failures, ROUND(100.0*SUM(tf)/COUNT(*),4) AS terminal_failure_pct FROM opf GROUP BY build_code ORDER BY build_code;",
 base + "SELECT period, region_code, class_code, build_code, COUNT(*) AS operations, SUM(tf) AS terminal_failures, ROUND(100.0*SUM(tf)/COUNT(*),4) AS terminal_failure_pct FROM opf GROUP BY period, region_code, class_code, build_code ORDER BY period, region_code, class_code, build_code;",
 base + ", cell AS (SELECT period, region_code, class_code, build_code, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(tf) AS f, 100.0*SUM(tf)/COUNT(*) AS p FROM opf GROUP BY period, region_code, class_code, build_code) SELECT build_code, COUNT(*) AS matched_slices, ROUND(AVG(p),4) AS standardized_failure_pct FROM cell GROUP BY build_code ORDER BY build_code;",
 base + ", cell AS (SELECT period, region_code, class_code, build_code, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(tf) AS f, 100.0*SUM(tf)/COUNT(*) AS p FROM opf GROUP BY period, region_code, class_code, build_code) SELECT c.period, c.region_code, c.class_code, ROUND(c.p,4) AS cand_pct, ROUND(r.p,4) AS ref_pct, ROUND(c.p-r.p,4) AS diff_pp, CASE WHEN c.p>r.p THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS cand_worse FROM cell c JOIN cell r ON r.period=c.period AND r.region_code=c.region_code AND r.class_code=c.class_code AND r.build_code='idx-r18' WHERE c.build_code='idx-r19' ORDER BY 1,2,3;",
 base + "SELECT period, class_code, COUNT(*) AS operations, ROUND(100.0*COUNT(*)/SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY period),4) AS traffic_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(tf)/COUNT(*),4) AS terminal_failure_pct FROM opf GROUP BY period, class_code ORDER BY period, class_code;",
 base + "SELECT period, class_code, build_code, COUNT(*) AS operations, SUM(tf) AS terminal_failures, ROUND(100.0*SUM(tf)/COUNT(*),4) AS terminal_failure_pct FROM opf GROUP BY period, class_code, build_code ORDER BY period, class_code, build_code;",
]
con = sqlite3.connect('file:../data/current.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
for q in qs:
    rows = con.execute(q).fetchall()
    print(len(rows), rows[:20])
json.dump(qs, open('qs.json','w'))
EOF

A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Investigate ledger-sync on 2026-05-07, reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. For every period and serving physical pool report operations, terminal failures and percentage, attempts, failed attempts and percentage, retried operations, minimum/maximum applied deadline_ms, and mean queue_ms and execution_ms of the terminal attempt among terminally failed operations. Report means of every recorded telemetry signal for those pools and applied changes during 10:00–12:00 (kind, pool, effective time, before/after JSON strings). In assessment identify the strongest supported proximal explanation, the affected pool and failure increase in pp. Explicitly evaluate both a deadline-policy change and worker/queue pressure against the current evidence. Explain the remaining causal limitation.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

              WHEN o.opened_at_ms >= 1778151600000 AND o.opened_at_ms < 1778155200000 THEN 'incident_11_12' END AS period
  FROM logical_operations o

  JOIN route_assignments a ON a.route_id=o.route_id AND o.opened_at_ms>=a.effective_from_ms AND o.opened_at_ms<a.effective_to_ms
  JOIN worker_pools wp ON wp.pool_id=a.pool_id
  JOIN policy_profiles p ON p.profile_id=a.profile_id
  WHERE o.opened_at_ms >= 1778148000000 AND o.opened_at_ms < 1778155200000
),
att AS (
  SELECT ae.operation_id, COUNT(*) n_att, MAX(ae.attempt_no) last_no,
         SUM(fc.is_success=0) failed_att
  FROM attempt_events ae JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=ae.code_id
  GROUP BY ae.operation_id
)

"assessment":("Strongest supported proximal explanation: the worker-concurrency limit on sync-south (pool 4) was cut from 16 to 4 at 2026-05-07 11:00 UTC, exactly at the start of the incident window. "
"In the same window sync-south telemetry shows available_workers falling 16->4 and queue_depth rising 4->180 (means over 12 samples each), while sync-north is unchanged on every signal. "
"sync-south terminal failures rose from 25 to 175 of 1000 operations (2.5% -> 17.5%, +15.0 percentage points); attempt failures rose from 15.22% to 46.77% (+31.55 pp). "
"All terminal failures are DEADLINE codes. Among terminally failed sync-south operations the terminal attempt's queue time rose from 5.0 ms to 235.0 ms while execution time fell from 245.0 ms to 15.0 ms, i.e. the 250 ms deadline was consumed by waiting for a worker, not by slow execution; upstream_latency_p95 was flat at 118 ms in both pools and periods. "
"Deadline-policy change: not supported. The ledger-sync routes resolve to profile balanced-250 (deadline 250 ms) for every operation in both periods (min=max=250). The only deadline_policy changes in change_events (2026-05-02) apply to parcel-index service pool 1 and occur outside the window; no deadline change touches ledger-sync or sync-south. Sync-north has the same 250 ms deadline and no failure increase, which argues against a global deadline effect. "

Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Report ledger-sync reliability for 2026-05-09: reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. Report the authoritative event source for these windows (registry version, event table, event grain and effective start). For each period and actual serving PHYSICAL pool, report logical operations, terminal failures, terminal-failure percentage, retried operations, retry percentage and mean end-to-end latency_ms. Do not treat routing intent or an individual execution identity as a physical pool. Also give all-pool operations, terminal failures and terminal-failure percentage per period; identify the physical pool with the largest increase and report that increase in pp. In assessment state what the report establishes and the important attribution/counting limitations.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE execution_cells(cell_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, cell_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE outcome_events(outcome_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES logical_operations, cell_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES execution_cells, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, final_code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, attempt_count INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_count>=1), total_queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(total_queue_ms>=0), total_execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(total_execution_ms>=0), total_backoff_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(total_backoff_ms>=0));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);
CREATE INDEX outcomes_cell ON outcome_events(cell_id,operation_id);

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

Then report those same five counts for each service, plus its terminal-failure percentage and the number of distinct serving physical pools represented in the window. Explain briefly in caveats why attempts and terminal failures are not interchangeable. This is a counting calibration, not an incident attribution exercise.

# Operations analytics data contract

You receive `current.db` (SQLite), this README and one task. Inspect the database schema, foreign keys and registry yourself. No network or external data is needed. The database is read-only input; use a read-only connection. All observations are synthetic, internally consistent and complete for the requested windows. Do not interpret absent windows as zero traffic. No hidden business definitions depend on an earlier task.

* Times ending `_ms` are integer Unix milliseconds in UTC. Window membership uses the **logical operation open time**, with inclusive lower and exclusive upper bounds. Effective intervals are also half-open; a NULL end means no known end.
* One logical operation is one business request. Retries are attempts, not extra incidents or requests. A terminal failure means the final attempt/outcome has a failure code whose `is_success` is 0; an earlier failed attempt followed by success is not a terminal failure. All included operations are finished and attempt ordinals are complete. An operation with more than one attempt is a retried operation, including ultimately failed operations.
* `feed_registry` is authoritative about event sources, grains, applicable operation-open intervals and serving attribution. The active entry describes current instrumentation; historical entries remain authoritative for their historical intervals. Do not assume the highest version covers all history or that a still-queryable table is current. Historical values are retained without rewriting them into a new meaning.
* Routing identifiers are routing intent, not necessarily unique physical pools. For routing-time instrumentation, select the assignment effective when the operation opens. For execution-time instrumentation, recorded execution attribution is authoritative. Multiple aliases or execution identities may belong to the same physical pool. Never count each identity as an independent pool.
* End-to-end latency is final completion minus operation open, including queueing, execution and retry backoff. Per-attempt queue/execution times exclude backoff. Outcome totals cover all its attempts. Rates use logical-operation denominators unless a task explicitly asks for attempt metrics. Percentages are in percent (0–100); rate differences are percentage points.
* Telemetry is sampled independently. A requested window mean is the ordinary arithmetic mean of samples in that window. An upstream p95 sample is a percentile observation, not an operation-weighted mean. Changes describe applied configuration, not a causal experiment. Tenant tier, operation class, release, region and pool are distinct dimensions.

Return only the JSON requested in the task: `answer`, `evidence_sql` (a list of executable, read-only SQLite SELECT/WITH statements supporting the answer), and `caveats` (a list of short strings). No placeholders, SQL parameters, temporary tables or external files in evidence. State uncertainty; observational association alone does not prove causation.

CREATE TABLE subsystems(subsystem_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE services(service_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, service_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE regions(region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenant_tiers(tier_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tier_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE tenants(tenant_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, tier_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_tiers);
CREATE TABLE worker_pools(pool_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES regions, pool_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE policy_profiles(profile_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, deadline_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(deadline_ms>0), max_attempts INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(max_attempts>=1));
CREATE TABLE failure_codes(code_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, is_success INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(is_success IN (0,1)), description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE releases(release_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, build_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_kinds(kind_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE change_events(change_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, effective_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, kind_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES change_kinds, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, pool_id INTEGER REFERENCES worker_pools, before_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(before_json)), after_json TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(json_valid(after_json)), change_note TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE service_routes(route_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, service_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES services, route_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE route_assignments(assignment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES policy_profiles, release_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES releases, CHECK(effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms), UNIQUE(route_id,effective_from_ms));
CREATE TABLE operation_classes(class_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, class_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE logical_operations(operation_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants, route_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES service_routes, class_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES operation_classes, opened_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE attempt_events(attempt_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES logical_operations, attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(attempt_no>=1), started_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, completed_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, code_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES failure_codes, queue_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(queue_ms>=0), execution_ms INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(execution_ms>=0), CHECK(completed_at_ms-started_at_ms=queue_ms+execution_ms), UNIQUE(operation_id,attempt_no));
CREATE TABLE telemetry_signals(signal_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, signal_code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, unit TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE telemetry_samples(sample_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pool_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES worker_pools, signal_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES telemetry_signals, measured_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, value REAL NOT NULL, UNIQUE(pool_id,signal_id,measured_at_ms));
CREATE TABLE incident_windows(incident_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, incident_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, subsystem_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES subsystems, start_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, end_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, report_summary TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(end_ms>start_ms));
CREATE TABLE feed_registry(version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_table TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, event_grain TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(event_grain IN ('attempt','operation')), effective_from_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, effective_to_ms INTEGER, lifecycle TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lifecycle IN ('active','historical')), operation_key_column TEXT NOT NULL, attribution_basis TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK(effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>effective_from_ms));
CREATE INDEX ops_open ON logical_operations(opened_at_ms,route_id);
CREATE INDEX attempts_operation ON attempt_events(operation_id,attempt_no DESC);
CREATE INDEX assignments_effective ON route_assignments(route_id,effective_from_ms,effective_to_ms);
CREATE INDEX samples_window ON telemetry_samples(measured_at_ms,pool_id,signal_id);

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Investigate parcel-index on 2026-05-02, comparing reference 10:00–11:00 with incident 11:00–12:00. For every period and serving physical pool, report operations, terminal failures and their percentage, attempts, failed attempts and their percentage, retried operations, and minimum/maximum applied deadline_ms. Report ordinary window means of every recorded telemetry signal for those pools, and applied changes during 10:00–12:00 (kind, pool, effective time, before/after JSON strings). In assessment, identify the most strongly supported proximal explanation, the affected pool and the terminal-failure increase in percentage points; contrast it with at least one plausible alternative. Distinguish evidence from causal proof. Attribute configuration at the time the operation entered the system, not from today's configuration.

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Evaluate parcel-index during early 2026-05-04 00:00–01:00 and late 2026-05-05 00:00–01:00. Candidate build is idx-r19 and reference is idx-r18. (1) For each period report operations, terminal failures, failure percentage, and candidate traffic percentage. (2) Pool both periods and report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage per build. (3) Report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage for each period × region × operation-class × build cell. These define eight matched slices (period × region × operation class), each containing both builds. (4) Standardize each build by giving those eight slices equal weight; report both standardized failure percentages, candidate minus reference in pp, and the number of slices where candidate is worse. (5) Report period × operation-class traffic shares and failure percentages. In assessment, explain whether the time trend and pooled build comparison support the claim “expanding the candidate improved reliability.” Identify the strongest measured association and distinguish a possible root-cause hypothesis from causal identification. Do not extrapolate beyond the observed strata. Equal weighting here is the specified target population, not weighting by observed build traffic.

bash
cat >> /tmp/analysis.sql <<'SQL'
WITH b AS (SELECT o.operation_id,CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms<1777939200000 THEN 'early' ELSE 'late' END period,c.class_code FROM logical_operations o JOIN service_routes sr USING(route_id) JOIN services s USING(service_id) JOIN operation_classes c USING(class_id) WHERE s.service_code='parcel-index' AND ((o.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777856400000) OR (o.opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1777942800000)), ops AS (SELECT b.*,f.is_success FROM b JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id=b.operation_id AND a.attempt_no=(SELECT max(attempt_no) FROM attempt_events x WHERE x.operation_id=b.operation_id) JOIN failure_codes f USING(code_id)) SELECT period,class_code,count(*) n,100.0*count(*)/(select count(*) from ops z where z.period=ops.period) traffic,100.0*sum(is_success=0)/count(*) pct FROM ops GROUP BY period,class_code;
SQL
sqlite3 -header -column ../data/current.db < <(tail -n 1 /tmp/analysis.sql)
exit 1; shell 0.01 s

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Investigate ledger-sync on 2026-05-07, reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. For every period and serving physical pool report operations, terminal failures and percentage, attempts, failed attempts and percentage, retried operations, minimum/maximum applied deadline_ms, and mean queue_ms and execution_ms of the terminal attempt among terminally failed operations. Report means of every recorded telemetry signal for those pools and applied changes during 10:00–12:00 (kind, pool, effective time, before/after JSON strings). In assessment identify the strongest supported proximal explanation, the affected pool and failure increase in pp. Explicitly evaluate both a deadline-policy change and worker/queue pressure against the current evidence. Explain the remaining causal limitation.

WITH base AS (SELECT o.operation_id,o.opened_at_ms,CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms<1778151600000 THEN 'reference' ELSE 'incident' END period,a.pool_id,pp.deadline_ms FROM logical_operations o JOIN service_routes r USING(route_id) JOIN services s USING(service_id) JOIN route_assignments a ON a.route_id=o.route_id AND o.opened_at_ms>=a.effective_from_ms AND o.opened_at_ms<a.effective_to_ms JOIN policy_profiles pp USING(profile_id) WHERE s.service_code='ledger-sync' AND o.opened_at_ms>=1778148000000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1778155200000), opstats AS (SELECT b.*,count(a.attempt_id) attempts,sum(CASE WHEN f.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) failed_attempts,max(a.attempt_no) max_no,max(CASE WHEN a.attempt_no=(select max(x.attempt_no) from attempt_events x where x.operation_id=b.operation_id) THEN f.is_success END) final_success,max(CASE WHEN a.attempt_no=(select max(x.attempt_no) from attempt_events x where x.operation_id=b.operation_id) THEN a.queue_ms END) terminal_queue,max(CASE WHEN a.attempt_no=(select max(x.attempt_no) from attempt_events x where x.operation_id=b.operation_id) THEN a.execution_ms END) terminal_execution FROM base b LEFT JOIN attempt_events a USING(operation_id) LEFT JOIN failure_codes f USING(code_id) GROUP BY b.operation_id) SELECT period,p.pool_code,count(*) operations,sum(final_success=0) failures,100.0*sum(final_success=0)/count(*) pct,sum(attempts) attempts,sum(failed_attempts) failed_attempts,100.0*sum(failed_attempts)/sum(attempts) attemptpct,sum(max_no>1) retries,min(deadline_ms),max(deadline_ms),avg(CASE WHEN final_success=0 THEN terminal_queue END) qmean,avg(CASE WHEN final_success=0 THEN terminal_execution END) emean FROM opstats JOIN worker_pools p USING(pool_id) GROUP BY period,p.pool_id;

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Report ledger-sync reliability for 2026-05-09: reference 10:00–11:00 versus incident 11:00–12:00. Report the authoritative event source for these windows (registry version, event table, event grain and effective start). For each period and actual serving PHYSICAL pool, report logical operations, terminal failures, terminal-failure percentage, retried operations, retry percentage and mean end-to-end latency_ms. Do not treat routing intent or an individual execution identity as a physical pool. Also give all-pool operations, terminal failures and terminal-failure percentage per period; identify the physical pool with the largest increase and report that increase in pp. In assessment state what the report establishes and the important attribution/counting limitations.

These figures should not be interpreted as attempt-event counts: the authoritative feed is operation-grain, and retries are reflected in its attempt_count."},"caveats":["The feed registry identifies from the actual execution cell recorded on each outcome, not the route assignment."] ,"evidence_sql":["SELECT version,event_table,event_grain,effective_from_ms FROM feed_registry WHERE effective_from_ms<=1778320800000 AND (effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>1778320800000) AND effective_from_ms<1778328000000 AND (effective_to_ms IS NULL OR effective_to_ms>=1778328000000);","WITH base AS (SELECT o.operation_id,o.opened_at_ms,CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms<1778324400000 THEN 'reference' ELSE 'incident' END AS period,c.pool_id,e.attempt_count,f.is_success,e.completed_at_ms-o.opened_at_ms AS latency_ms FROM logical_operations o JOIN outcome_events e ON e.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN execution_cells c ON c.cell_id=e.cell_id JOIN services s ON s.service_id=c.service_id JOIN failure_codes f ON f.code_id=e.final_code_id WHERE s.service_code='ledger-sync' AND o.opened_at_ms>=1778320800000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1778328000000) SELECT period,p.pool_code,COUNT(*) AS operations,SUM(CASE WHEN is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS terminal_failures,100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) AS terminal_failure_pct,SUM(CASE WHEN attempt_count>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retried_operations,100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN attempt_count>1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) AS retry_pct,AVG(latency_ms) AS mean_latency_ms FROM base JOIN worker_pools p ON p.pool_id=base.pool_id GROUP BY period,base.pool_id ORDER BY period,p.pool_code;","SELECT CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms<1778324400000 THEN 'reference' ELSE 'incident' END AS period,COUNT(*) AS operations,SUM(CASE WHEN f.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS terminal_failures,100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN f.is_success=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*) AS terminal_failure_pct FROM logical_operations o JOIN outcome_events e ON e.operation_id=o.operation_id JOIN execution_cells c ON c.cell_id=e.cell_id JOIN services s ON s.service_id=c.service_id JOIN failure_codes f ON f.code_id=e.final_code_id WHERE s.service_code='ledger-sync' AND o.opened_at_ms>=1778320800000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1778328000000 GROUP BY period ORDER BY period;"]}

WITH base AS (SELECT o.operation_id,o.opened_at_ms,CASE WHEN o.opened_at_ms<1778324400000 THEN 'reference' ELSE 'incident' END period,oc.pool_id,oc.cell_id,oe.attempt_count,fc.is_success,(oe.completed_at_ms-o.opened_at_ms) latency FROM logical_operations o JOIN outcome_events oe USING(operation_id) JOIN execution_cells oc USING(cell_id) JOIN services s ON s.service_id=oc.service_id JOIN worker_pools p USING(pool_id) JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=oe.final_code_id WHERE s.service_code='ledger-sync' AND o.opened_at_ms>=1778320800000 AND o.opened_at_ms<1778328000000), agg AS (SELECT period,pool_id,count(*) operations,sum(is_success=0) failures,sum(attempt_count>1) retried,avg(latency) latency FROM base GROUP BY period,pool_id) SELECT period,pool_code,operations,failures,100.0*failures/operations pct,retried,100.0*retried/operations retry_pct,latency FROM agg JOIN worker_pools USING(pool_id);
SELECT CASE WHEN opened_at_ms<1778324400000 THEN 'reference' ELSE 'incident' END period,count(*) operations,sum(fc.is_success=0) failures,100.0*sum(fc.is_success=0)/count(*) pct FROM logical_operations o JOIN outcome_events e USING(operation_id) JOIN execution_cells c USING(cell_id) JOIN services s ON s.service_id=c.service_id JOIN failure_codes fc ON fc.code_id=e.final_code_id WHERE s.service_code='ledger-sync' AND opened_at_ms>=1778320800000 AND opened_at_ms<1778328000000 GROUP BY period;

Постановка задачи
Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

For 2026-05-01 10:00–11:00, report total logical operations, attempts, failed attempts, terminal failures, and retried operations across all services. Then report those same five counts for each service, plus its terminal-failure percentage and the number of distinct serving physical pools represented in the window. Explain briefly in caveats why attempts and terminal failures are not interchangeable. This is a counting calibration, not an incident attribution exercise.

    "WITH ops AS (SELECT o.operation_id, o.route_id, o.opened_at_ms FROM logical_operations o WHERE o.opened_at_ms >= 1777629600000 AND o.opened_at_ms < 1777633200000), per_op AS (SELECT ops.operation_id, COUNT(a.attempt_id) AS attempts, SUM(CASE WHEN f.is_success = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_attempts, MAX(CASE WHEN a.attempt_no = (SELECT MAX(a2.attempt_no) FROM attempt_events a2 WHERE a2.operation_id = ops.operation_id) AND f.is_success = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS terminal_failure FROM ops JOIN attempt_events a ON a.operation_id = ops.operation_id JOIN failure_codes f ON f.code_id = a.code_id GROUP BY ops.operation_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS operations, SUM(attempts) AS attempts, SUM(failed_attempts) AS failed_attempts, SUM(terminal_failure) AS terminal_failures, SUM(CASE WHEN attempts > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retried_operations FROM per_op;",
